Specify newborn group identity inheritance

Source: R/group_inheritance.R
group_inheritance.Rd

A model specification indicating how the group category of newborns should be assigned for a particular group dimension. Used in group().

Usage

group_inheritance(
  method = "random_parent",
  fun = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  passing = 0,
  fixed_value = NULL
)

Arguments

method

One of "mother", "father", "random_parent", "same_sex", "opposite_sex", "ancestry", "fixed", "hierarchy", or "custom". See details for further information.

fun

For "custom", an R function defined by the user. See details for variables exposed for this function.

order

For "hierarchy", unique group labels, highest-ranked first. Chooses between parental group membership, not ancestry.

passing

For "hierarchy", probability in [0,1] of reversing the order for a birth. Defaults to zero.

fixed_value

For "fixed", one category label or finite numeric code in the dimension's categories. Every newborn receives this category.

Value

An inspectable hammel_group_inheritance object.

Details

Whenever groups are in use, an inheritance rule is required to determine how the group membership of newborns is determined. The function provides several out of the box methods, as well as the ability for users to define a custom method:

  • random_parent: The default method. The newborn is assigned the group membership of a randomly selected parent with equal probability.

  • mother - The newborn is assigned the group membership of the mother.

  • father - The newborn is assigned the group membership of the father.

  • same_sex - The newborn is assigned the group membership of their same-sex parent.

  • different_sex - The newborn is assigned the group membership of their opposite-sex parent.

  • ancestry - The newborn is assigned a group membership randomly, weighted by their ancestry share from each group. ancestry = TRUE must be set for the group to use this method.

  • fixed - All newborns are assigned a fixed group membership given by the fixed_value argument.

  • hierarchy - The newborn is assigned the group membership from the parent whose membership is higher on the order argument. If the passing argument is provided, it defines the probability that this ordering is inverted.

  • custom - The newborn is assigned a group membership based on a custom R function provided by the user with the fun argument. Simulations with custom R functions are slower to process.

For methods that require no additional arguments (random_parent, mother, father, same_sex, different_sex, ancestry), the name of the method may be passed to arguments requiring an inheritance model like group() instead of the model itself.

For the custom function, the following variables are exposed and can be called from the function declaration:

  • mother_group: The mother's group membership.

  • father_group: The father's group membership. NA if unknown.

  • mother_ancestry: Numeric vector of ancestry share from each group for mother, as well as an "unknown" value for unknown ancestry.

  • father_ancestry: Numeric vector of ancestry share from each group for father, as well as an "unknown" value for unknown ancestry.

  • child_ancestry: Numeric vector of ancestry share from each group for child, as well as an "unknown" value for unknown ancestry.

  • child_sex: Either "f" or "m".

  • parents_in_union: Logical indicating whether the parents were in a union, including on-demand union formation.

Examples

group_inheritance("fixed", fixed_value = "none")
#> $method
#> [1] "fixed"
#> 
#> $fun
#> NULL
#> 
#> $order
#> NULL
#> 
#> $passing
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $fixed_value
#> [1] "none"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "hammel_group_inheritance"
group_inheritance("mother")
#> $method
#> [1] "mother"
#> 
#> $fun
#> NULL
#> 
#> $order
#> NULL
#> 
#> $passing
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $fixed_value
#> NULL
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "hammel_group_inheritance"
group_inheritance("hierarchy", order = c("B", "W"), passing = 0.05)
#> $method
#> [1] "hierarchy"
#> 
#> $fun
#> NULL
#> 
#> $order
#> [1] "B" "W"
#> 
#> $passing
#> [1] 0.05
#> 
#> $fixed_value
#> NULL
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "hammel_group_inheritance"
group_inheritance("custom",
  fun = function(mother_group, father_group, ...) {
    if (is.na(father_group) || mother_group == father_group) {
      mother_group
    } else {
      "mixed"
    }
  }
)
#> $method
#> [1] "custom"
#> 
#> $fun
#> function (mother_group, father_group, ...) 
#> {
#>     if (is.na(father_group) || mother_group == father_group) {
#>         mother_group
#>     }
#>     else {
#>         "mixed"
#>     }
#> }
#> <environment: 0x5b109602bfb0>
#> 
#> $order
#> NULL
#> 
#> $passing
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $fixed_value
#> NULL
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "hammel_group_inheritance"
